text.p: The Federal Trade Commission is preparing to reject Ameritech Corp's application to offer long-distance phone service in Michigan, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
The formal rejection is expected early next week, the paper said in its electronic edition.
The rejection is likely to offer the first detailed look at what the FTC believes the Baby Bells must do to gain entry to the long-distance business, the paper said.
Last year's telecommunications law cleared the way for the Baby Bells to enter the long-distance business where they can show they opened up their markets to local competitors.

In the FTC's first formal consideration of such a request, it rejected SBC Communications' bid to offer long-distance services in Oklahoma but offered little guidance on what it thinks the Baby Bells must do to prove they have opened their markets, the paper said.
